headline_marked: Google Launches [[SynthID Website]] to Detect AI-Generated Media
headline: Google Launches SynthID Website to Detect AI-Generated Media
summary: Google's new SynthID tool is now publicly available, allowing anyone to check if images, videos, or audio clips were created by AI. The site supports a wide range of file formats.
details: Google has officially launched a new website powered by its SynthID technology, enabling users to identify AI-generated media. This tool, previously in testing, now supports various image, video, and audio file formats, making it accessible for public use.

SynthID works by embedding digital watermarks into AI-generated content. These watermarks are designed to be imperceptible to humans but detectable by SynthID's technology, even after common transformations. This ensures robust identification of media produced by generative AI.

The technology is integrated with Google's own AI models like Nano Banana, Veo, and Lyria, as well as tools such as Gemini and Flow. Companies like OpenAI, NVIDIA, and Kakao also support SynthID, with Apple reportedly planning to add support soon.

Google has already incorporated SynthID verification into its Gemini app and Google Chrome browser. The company reports that approximately one million requests to verify content are made daily, highlighting the growing need for such detection tools in the digital landscape.
